item.title: How will tariffs affect the midterms? In this Michigan border town, it's complicated
item.description: The recent trade war between the U.S. and Canada has both economic and political implications for Michigan given it's the state's top trade partner.

item.title: ICE detainee dies just hours after he was admitted into detention
item.description: Lianyong Wei's death marks the 57th death of an immigrant detainee held in the care of the government since the start of President Trump's second term. Twenty-four of those have occurred since Jan. 1.

item.title: Whistleblower claims USPS plan for Trump's mail voting order could disrupt midterms
item.description: An anonymous federal official warned in a whistleblower complaint that a technical system the Postal Service built for mail voting is flawed and, if implemented, likely to disrupt the fall midterms.
item.content:encoded: An anonymous federal official warned in a whistleblower complaint that a technical system the Postal Service built for mail voting is flawed and, if implemented, likely to disrupt the fall midterms.

item.title: Attorney for whistleblower discusses claims about USPS mail-in voting system
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with attorney David Kligerman, who is representing a whistleblower who claims major discrepancies in a new U.S. Postal Service mail-in voting system.

item.title: Advocates say cities' aggressive clearing of encampments has caused more problems
item.description: A Supreme Court ruling two years ago allowed bans on sleeping outside. Homeless people and advocates in the Midwest say aggressive encampment clearing has caused problems.

item.title: How Dolly Parton's literacy work affected Indigenous communities in Australia
item.description: In Australia, the queen of country music, Dolly Parton, is being remembered for her work in advancing children's literacy, particularly in Indigenous communities.

item.title: The Clancy jury continues to deliberate
item.description: The jury in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the mother charged with murdering her three children, said it's not yet come to an unanimous decision. The judge has urged them to keep trying.

item.title: USPS 'carefully reviewing' whistleblower claim on plan for Trump's mail in voting order
item.description: A whistleblower says the U.S. Postal Service is rushing out an online system for President Trump's push to restrict mail voting that could "derail" the midterm election if courts allow it to proceed.

item.title: A makeover for college: No gym, no meal plan and two years of work
item.description: A new model in Vermont emphasizes hands-on learning while stripping away frills like gyms and meal plans that increase costs. Other newly created institutions are also reimagining college.
